transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood CSM), Mark (CTO), Jenna (Eng Mgr), Samir (Infra), Claire (Security)

Summary (auto): Short recap at top — see notes.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, quick round of intros?
[00:10] Mark: Hi I'm Mark, CTO at HorizonTech. We build a customer analytics product that uses long-form generation and reranking for insight reports.
[00:18] Jenna: Jenna, engineering manager on the ML infra team, I own serving and production pipelines.
[00:24] Samir: Samir, infra lead, I handle our VPC/networking and deployment stuff.
[00:28] Claire: Claire from security, I'll be the one asking the SOC2/KMS questions.
[00:33] Alex: Great. Priya, do you want to give a short overview of what we wanted to cover?
[00:37] Priya: Sure, thanks. We'll cover Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools, isolation options (VPC/private), burst strategies, how we handle autoscaling and tail latency, and a quick plan for a pilot. We'll also answer security questions.
[00:49] Mark: The high-level for us: we're deciding between Redwood Hosted and Dedicated. Main drivers are latency — p99 issues during peak — and data isolation. We also have regulatory customers that need stronger isolation. Cost is a factor but predictable latency is more important.
[01:05] Alex: Totally understood. Quick qual question: what does your traffic look like? QPS, typical sequence lengths, and any big daily peaks?
[01:14] Jenna: Average qps is about 12 rps, peak around 110 rps for short bursts — think 10-20 minute spikes tied to batch jobs and nightly report runs. Sequence lengths vary — most requests are 150-400 tokens but the reports can be 1K-2K tokens for the long generation flows.
[01:31] Samir: We also have internal async pipelines that can generate hundreds of parallel requests during backfill.
[01:38] Priya: Good context. For Dedicated we usually recommend sizing for sustained throughput plus a controlled burst buffer. We support dedicated GPU pools with autoscaling rules and a configurable burst cap — you can reserve N GPUs and allow bursting up to M additional capacity for short periods.
[01:54] Mark: Can you be specific — like how many GPUs for 110 rps? We were ballparking A100s but open to quantized options.
[02:02] Priya: Ballpark depends on model and quantization. For a 70B decoder model quantized to int8, a single A100 could serve roughly 10-20 rps with 1k average context under low-latency config; for your 1k-2k sequences, I would recommend planning ~6-8 A100s for sustained peak 110 rps if you want headroom and lower p99. But we can trade cost with throughput: mixed strategies where heavier requests go to Dedicated and smaller ones to Hosted or a smaller model variant.
[02:31] Jenna: Ok that matches our internal estimates. When you say burst, is that on-demand GPUs spun up in our pool or is it using shared capacity?
[02:38] Priya: It's shared in the sense that burst capacity can be backed by adjacent availability zones in the Redwood fleet or by compatible model variants on smaller GPUs. For Redwood Dedicated we guarantee your reserved pool (isolation), and bursts are provisioned from the cluster with policy-driven fallback. We also have an option to pre-warm burst nodes to reduce cold-starts.
[02:55] Claire: From a security standpoint, can burst nodes access our data or is there any cross-tenant leakage risk?
[03:02] Priya: Great question. For Dedicated, your reserved GPUs and data paths are isolated; burst nodes are only used when policy allows and we can enforce that burst instances run in tenant-isolated environments or on dedicated burst capacity depending on contract. We can also require encryption in transit and at rest, and use customer-managed keys.
[03:19] Claire: And KMS? We need to ensure no key material leaves our control.
[03:25] Alex: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM — you can bring your own key and we support envelope encryption. We'll share the crypto whitepaper.
[03:33] Mark: How about network topology — can we put Redwood Dedicated inside our VPC or do we have to use a private peering setup?
[03:41] Priya: We offer Private deployment with a customer-managed VPC option for Dedicated. There are two patterns: a private control plane + VPC peering or a full VPC-hosted deployment depending on your security needs. For strict compliance you can run a customer-managed private control plane in your account.
[03:56] Samir: Latency is key — what's the expected cold-start for a burst node versus an always-on reserved node?
[04:02] Priya: Reserved nodes are always warm; cold-start depends on model size and whether kernels are pre-loaded. With pre-warmed images we typically see <10s for large models; without pre-warm it can be 20-45s. We usually recommend pre-warming for customer-critical burst paths.
[04:18] Jenna: If we pre-warm, does that count towards our reserved capacity billing?
[04:22] Alex: Pre-warmed burst nodes are billable while allocated; policies can be tuned so pre-warmed nodes are smaller footprints or are only kept for short windows. We'll include pricing options in the deck.
[04:32] Mark: What about autoscale policies — how quickly can you scale back down to avoid runaway costs?
[04:38] Priya: Autoscale rules are policy-driven: scale by queue depth or CPU/GPU utilization with configurable cooldown windows. We support fast scale-up for latency SLOs and more conservative scale-down to avoid flapping. You can also set hard caps and time-based schedules.
[04:53] Samir: Can we self-host the control plane? We prefer our infra team to manage rollout and certs.
[04:58] Priya: Yes, for Private deployments we can give you a customer-managed control plane that lives in your VPC; that gives you certificate control and no cross-tenant control plane traffic.
[05:07] Claire: On compliance — do you provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation? We need audit reports.
[05:12] Alex: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant. We can share the SOC2 report under NDA and we also provide audit logs, retention controls, and SSO/SAML support.
[05:21] Claire: And RBAC?
[05:23] Priya: Yes, RBAC with SSO integrations, role bindings, and fine-grained token permissions.
[05:29] Mark: For the pilot, what should we measure? Latency p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and throughput under backfill seems right.
[05:37] Priya: Agreed. Also include failure modes — model fallback when capacity constrained, and KV/prefix cache hit rates. We'll propose a benchmark plan.
[05:45] Jenna: On model versions — we need canary and rollback for model updates.
[05:49] Alex: Rollouts are supported — canaries, A/B, and automatic fallback to previous model variant if quality drops.
[05:55] Mark: Any gotchas with quantized models and our evaluation metrics? We care about hallucination and generation quality for the long reports.
[06:02] Priya: Quantization can slightly affect generation quality; we recommend running evals. If you need identical logits for auditing, you should use a float variant in the Dedicated pool. We can set mixed model routing — higher-fidelity float models for audit paths, quantized variants for cost-sensitive flows.
[06:20] Samir: Networking question: do you support private endpoint inside our subnets with strict egress rules?
[06:26] Priya: Yes, private endpoints with enforced egress and optional NAT gateway configurations; we'll work with your infra team for IP allowlists and peering.
[06:34] Mark: How do you handle KV cache across replicas — consistency vs latency tradeoffs?
[06:40] Priya: We provide per-shard KV caches with replication strategies. For low-latency we keep warm KV local to the GPU serving the session; for stronger consistency we replicate writes across shards at slight latency cost.
[06:54] Jenna: We also want to throttle or route heavy batch backfills to lower-priority capacity so we don't impact online p99s.
[07:01] Priya: We can define QoS classes and route backfills to a separate dedicated queue or to a cheaper preemptible pool.
[07:07] Mark: Are preemptible GPU pools supported for cheaper burst capacity?
[07:11] Priya: Yes, preemptible/spot-backed pools are an option for non-critical workloads; we surface preemption risk and can checkpoint state where applicable.
[07:20] Samir: For billing predictability we want committed monthly capacity plus a small burst budget — do you do blended billing?
[07:26] Alex: Yes, committed reserved capacity with an overage rate for burst usage is standard; we can also do committed usage discounts for annual contracts. We'll provide a few pricing scenarios.
[07:36] Claire: Incident response — do you offer SOC/SLA incident reporting and postmortems?
[07:40] Luis: We provide SLA-backed incident reporting for Dedicated customers with a dedicated support channel and postmortem exports.
[07:47] Mark: Ok, let's talk timeline. We want a pilot in the next 3-4 weeks with a small production shadow for a month and then evaluate expansion.
[07:56] Alex: Sounds reasonable. For pilot we'll need your QPS data, sample prompts, and any special evals; we'll size a small Dedicated pool to replicate peak and run lat/throughput tests.
[08:08] Priya: We'll propose a bench plan: measure p50/p95/p99, cold-starts, tail lat under concurrency, and throughput for long sequences.
[08:16] Jenna: One operational question: do you expose token-level cost breakdowns per route? We want per-feature cost accountability.
[08:22] Alex: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level breakdowns, route tagging, and cost attribution.
[08:27] Mark: Great. A couple of smaller items — can we lock model weights for privacy so Redwood can't snapshot them?
[08:33] Priya: For Dedicated + Private we can enforce that model artifacts only live in your account or under encryption with customer keys. We'll detail options in the security doc.
[08:44] Claire: Ok will need to consult legal — but that sounds promising.
[08:47] Mark: Any limitations we should be aware of?
[08:50] Priya: The main tradeoffs are cost vs latency. Very large sequence lengths increase memory and reduce throughput. Also, burst-to-shared capacity depends on availability in the region — for strict guarantees choose fully private dedicated capacity.
[09:04] Jenna: For observability, can we get tracing hooks to correlate requests from our front-end to model responses?
[09:11] Luis: Yes, we provide tracing hooks and per-request tracing IDs, plus sampling options.
[09:17] Samir: Ok let's reconfirm the deliverables and timeline.
[09:20] Alex: Deliverables: pricing deck + Dedicated sizing doc (Alex), benchmark plan (Priya), customer logs and QPS histogram (Samir). Proposed pilot start: next Tuesday 10am PT.
[09:33] Mark: Sounds good.
[09:35] Jenna: Quick question — for model fallback, how is routing policy authored?
[09:39] Priya: It's a policy DSL in the console and via API: route by latency threshold, cost, or by feature flag. We'll include sample policies.
[09:47] (cross talk)
[09:50] Mark: Thanks all, that was helpful.
[09:53] Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll send the materials and get the pilot scheduled.
